verdict.rationale: Ardent documents a path for connecting an existing production Postgres database (Supabase, RDS, PlanetScale, self-hosted) as a connector. That path includes a preflight check, resumable setup and replicated isolated copies, framed as never touching production, so source downtime is implicitly minimal. However, this connects production as a branching source rather than migrating the production workload onto Ardent. missing for 10: an explicit documented migration/import guide with downtime guarantees, details on initial sync time for large databases, cutover steps, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can import an existing production database with minimal downtime using a documented migration path

citations.quote: Any Postgres — Supabase, RDS, PlanetScale, or self-hosted.
Preflight checks whether Ardent can branch this database. It creates nothing and stores no credentials — it just tells you what, if anything, to fix.
If it's interrupted, resume with: ardent connector retry-setup <name>
Ardent creates instant, isolated copies of your production Postgres database — in seconds, right from your terminal.
